script:
Anna: Hi, Tom. You look tired.
Tom: Yeah. My neighbors had a party last night, and I couldn't sleep.
Anna: That's terrible. Did you talk to them?
Tom: Not yet. I'm going to knock on their door tonight, but I don't want to sound angry.
Anna: Maybe you could take them some cookies. People are usually friendlier when you're nice.
Tom: That's actually a good idea. However, if the noise continues, I'll call the building manager.
Anna: Good plan. Let me know how it goes.

qs.q: What is Tom's problem?
opts: His neighbors were too noisy at night
He argued with the building manager
He had a party and cleaned up late
qs.why: He says the neighbors had a party and he couldn't sleep.

qs.q: What will Tom do tonight?
qs.why: He says he is going to knock on their door tonight. Calling the manager is only a backup plan.

qs.q: What does Anna imply with 'People are usually friendlier when you're nice'?
opts: Tom should call the manager first
A kind approach may work better than anger
qs.why: She suggests being nice is more effective than sounding angry.

script: Attention, please, passengers travelling to Edinburgh on flight BA 214. Due to a technical problem, the departure gate has changed from gate twelve to gate twenty-five. The flight will now leave at ten forty instead of ten fifteen. Please make your way to the new gate as soon as possible. Passengers who need help can ask any member of staff. qs.why: 'Make your way to' means to go to a place.

script: Hi Sara, it's Dave from the IT team. I'm calling about your laptop. We tried to fix the problem remotely, but it didn't work, so I'm afraid you'll have to bring it to the help desk. It's on the second floor, next to the cafeteria. We're open from nine to five, but don't come at lunchtime because it gets really busy. Also, please back up your files before you come. Otherwise, you might lose some of them. Call me back if you have any questions. Thanks.

To ask Sara to bring her laptop to the help desk

qs.q: What will happen if Sara doesn't back up her files?
opts: She might lose some of them
qs.why: 'Otherwise, you might lose some of them.'

script: I used to hate mornings, but things have changed since I started running. I get up at six, put on my trainers and run for thirty minutes before work. At first, it was hard, so I gave up after three days. Then my sister joined me, and we kept each other going. Now I feel more energetic, and I even enjoy breakfast! The only problem is the winter. When it's dark and cold, it's tempting to stay in bed.

qs.q: What is the speaker mainly talking about?
opts: How to cook a better breakfast
qs.why: She describes how her mornings improved after she started running.

qs.q: What helped the speaker keep running?
qs.why: Her sister joined her, and they kept each other going.

qs.q: What does the speaker imply about winter?
opts: It is the hardest season to keep the habit
Dark mornings are exciting for her
qs.why: Dark, cold mornings make her tempted to stay in bed.

script:

Jake: Sure! What's the plan?
Lisa: We're meeting at my place at six. Her husband will bring her at seven, so we have to be quiet.
Jake: Should I bring a gift?
Lisa: You don't have to, but a small card would be nice. Oh, and don't mention it to Maria. She finds out about everything.

script: The city council has approved a plan to build twenty-five miles of new bike lanes over the next two years. The mayor said the project will cost around twelve million dollars, and most of the money will come from the national government. Supporters say the lanes will reduce traffic and pollution. A bike race will be held

script:
Karen: I've just heard the client wants the report by Thursday instead of Friday.
Paul: Thursday? That's impossible. We still have to finish the charts.
Karen: I know. But if we split the work, we might pull it off. I'll handle the summary if you take care of the data.
Paul: Fine, although I'll probably have to stay late tonight.

Paul: Agreed. Otherwise we'll end up redoing everything.

qs.q: What does Paul imply with 'Otherwise we'll end up redoing everything'?
opts: Checking the numbers early avoids mistakes later
He wants to skip tomorrow's meeting

script: So, here's the thing about passwords. Most people reuse the same one everywhere, and that's a huge risk. If one website gets hacked, criminals can try it on your email, your bank, everything. That's why I'd strongly recommend using a password manager. It creates a different password for each site, and you only have to remember one. Sure, it takes a bit of time to set up, but it's worth it. And turn on two-step verification too. Even if somebody figures out your password, they still can't get in.

qs.q: What is the speaker's main point?
opts: How to remember many passwords by heart
Why a password manager and two-step verification improve security
qs.why: He recommends both tools to protect accounts.

qs.q: What does a password manager do?
opts: It creates a different password for each site
It removes the need for an email account
qs.why: It creates a different password for each site.

qs.q: What does 'figures out' mean in 'Even if somebody figures out your password'?
qs.why: To figure out something is to discover or understand it.

script:

Almost sixty percent of employees said they would look for a new job if their company forced them to return to the office full time. A new bakery opening next year

script:
Anna: Did you see the alert this morning?
Mark: Yes. The database stopped responding around nine, and half the app went down with it.
Anna: Do we know why?
Mark: At first we blamed a bad deployment, so we rolled it back. That didn't help. It turned out to be a network issue between two data centers.
Anna: So the root cause wasn't our code. As long as the backups are fine, we haven't lost anything.
Mark: Well, the last full backup was Sunday, so I wouldn't say that just yet.

qs.q: What was the main problem?

A network issue stopped the database from responding
qs.why: The database stopped responding because of a network issue.

qs.q: What does 'turned out' mean when Mark says 'It turned out to be a network issue'?

qs.q: What does Mark imply about the backup?
opts: Some recent data may have been lost
The backup was deleted on purpose
qs.why: The last full backup was Sunday, so newer data might be missing.

script: When we started the company, we thought raising money would be the hard part. Turns out, it wasn't. What really caught us off guard was hiring. We'd get a fantastic candidate, and then they'd turn us down because a bigger firm offered them double. So we had to rethink our approach. Instead of competing on salary, we put the emphasis on ownership and learning. People could work on real projects from day one. It's not for everyone, but the folks who stayed are some of the most committed I've ever worked with.

qs.q: What was the hardest part for the company?
qs.why: Hiring caught them off guard, not fundraising.

qs.q: What does 'turn us down' mean?
qs.why: Candidates rejected the job offers.

qs.q: What does the speaker imply about the people who stayed?
qs.why: He calls them some of the most committed people he has worked with.

script: Thousands of passengers face disruption this weekend after pilots at a major European airline voted to go on strike. The union says the walkout, which is due to begin on Friday, is a response to stalled talks over pay and working hours. The airline insists it has made a fair offer and has urged the union to come back to the table. Meanwhile, travellers have been advised to check their flight status before heading to the airport. Analysts warn that if the dispute drags on, it could cost the company millions.

qs.q: What is the news mainly about?
opts: Pilots plan a strike over pay and working hours
Airports will close for a week
qs.why: Pilots voted to strike after stalled talks.

qs.q: When is the strike due to begin?
qs.why: The walkout is due to begin on Friday.

qs.q: What does 'drags on' suggest about the dispute?
opts: It continues for a long time
qs.why: 'Drag on' means to continue for too long.

script:
Emma: Can we talk? I've been putting this off for weeks.
Dan: Sure. Is everything okay?
Emma: Well, I've been offered a job in Seattle, and I'm seriously thinking about taking it.
Dan: Wow. I didn't see that coming. What about us?
Emma: That's what's been keeping me up at night. I don't want to break up, but I can't turn this down either.
Dan: Look, I'm not going to pretend I'm thrilled. But I'd never ask you to give up something you've worked so hard for.
Emma: Thank you. Maybe we could try long-distance for a year and see how it goes.

qs.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
opts: Emma has a job offer in another city
Emma is breaking up with Dan
qs.why: Emma has been offered a job in Seattle.

qs.q: What does Dan mean by 'I didn't see that coming'?
qs.why: The phrase means the news was unexpected.

qs.q: How does Dan feel?
opts: Angry and ready to end it
qs.why: He's not thrilled but says he'd never ask her to give up the job.

script: Hello, this is a message for Mr Patel from Swift Couriers. We tried to deliver your parcel this morning, but unfortunately nobody was home. We'll attempt delivery again tomorrow between two and six in the afternoon. If you can't be there, you can either arrange for a neighbour to sign for it or collect it from our depot on Hill Road until Friday. After that, the parcel will be sent back to the sender. To reschedule, please call us on the number on your delivery card, quoting reference seven-four-one-nine.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the message?
opts: To say a parcel was lost
To explain a failed delivery and the options available
To say the driver is on strike
qs.why: The delivery failed, and Mr Patel is given options.

qs.q: Until when can Mr Patel collect the parcel from the depot?
qs.why: He can collect it until Friday; after that it goes back.

qs.q: What does 'sign for it' mean?
opts: write a name to confirm receipt
qs.why: A neighbour can confirm receipt with a signature.

script: I've been using AI assistants at work for about a year now, and honestly, my opinion keeps changing. At first I was blown away. It could draft emails, summarize reports, even write code in seconds. But then I noticed I was relying on it too much, and I'd stopped double-checking its answers. That came back to bite me when a made-up statistic ended up in a client presentation. These days I treat it like a smart intern: great for a first draft, but nothing leaves my desk until I've gone over it myself.

qs.q: How does the speaker describe his experience?
opts: His view became more careful over time
He wants to build AI tools
qs.why: His opinion changed from amazement to careful use.

qs.q: What does 'came back to bite me' mean?
qs.why: His lack of checking later caused trouble.

qs.q: What does 'a smart intern' suggest about how he treats AI output?
opts: He checks it before using it
He sends it straight to clients
qs.why: Nothing leaves his desk until he has reviewed it.

script:
Helen: I appreciate you meeting us at such short notice.
Omar: Not at all. I'll be upfront, though. The figures you sent over are well above our budget.
Helen: I understand. That said, the price reflects the level of support we provide, which is round the clock.
Omar: Right, but we barely need that. Could you come down on the price if we dropped it to office hours only?
Helen: I'd have to run that by my director, but I don't see why not. Realistically, we could knock around fifteen percent off.
Omar: That would make it easier to sell internally. Let's put something in writing by Friday.

qs.q: What are Helen and Omar discussing?
opts: The price of a support contract
qs.why: They negotiate the price of round-the-clock support.

qs.q: What does 'run that by my director' mean?
opts: check it with her director first
qs.why: She needs her director's approval before agreeing.

qs.q: What does 'I don't see why not' imply?

qs.why: It signals she expects the director to accept.

script: Housing costs continue to outpace wages in most major cities, according to a report released on Tuesday. Researchers found that the average renter now spends nearly forty percent of their income on housing, which is well above the level economists consider sustainable. The report attributes the trend largely to a shortage of new construction, compounded by rising interest rates. Some officials are pushing to relax zoning laws so that developers can build more apartments. Critics, however, caution that without stronger tenant protections, such measures may do little to ease the burden on lower-income families.

qs.q: What is the report's main finding?
opts: Rents have dropped in most cities
Housing costs are rising faster than wages
qs.why: 'Outpace' means housing costs are growing faster than wages.

qs.q: What share of income does the average renter spend on housing?
qs.why: The report says nearly forty percent.

qs.q: What do the critics imply?
opts: Easing zoning alone may not help poorer families enough
qs.why: They say relaxed zoning may do little without tenant protections.

script: People often ask me how I manage to see so many countries on a budget. The truth is, I don't try to see everything. I used to rush from city to city, ticking off sights, and I came home exhausted. Now I stay in one place for at least a week. That way, I get to know the neighbourhood, find the cheap local restaurants and even pick up a little of the language. Admittedly, I miss out on some famous attractions, but I'd rather understand one place properly than glance at ten.

qs.q: How has the speaker's way of travelling changed?
opts: He visits ten cities a week
He now stays longer in each place
qs.why: He now stays at least a week in one place.

qs.q: What is the minimum time he stays in one place?
qs.why: He says he stays for at least a week.

qs.q: What does 'miss out on' suggest?
opts: He doesn't get to experience some attractions
qs.why: 'Miss out on' means lose the chance to experience something.

I was trying to be helpful, but looking back, it came across as patronizing. You'd have every right to be annoyed. Anyway, I'd love to make it up to you. Dinner's on me if you're up for it. And if you'd rather not talk for a while, I totally get it. Just know I'm sorry.

qs.why: He apologizes for mentioning her job situation in public.

qs.why: 'Dinner's on me' means he will pay.

script:

Tom: Which part concerns you?
Priya: The timeline. Moving everything to the cloud in six weeks seems wildly optimistic, especially with half the team on leave in August.
Tom: Fair point. We could phase it, starting with the non-critical services, and leave the payment system until last.
Priya: That would reduce the risk considerably. But I'd want a rollback plan for every phase, not just a vague promise.
Tom: Understood. I'll revise the proposal and circulate it before Thursday's review.

qs.q: What is Priya's main concern?
opts: She wants to hire more people
qs.why: She thinks six weeks is wildly optimistic.

qs.q: What does Tom suggest?

qs.why: He proposes a phased approach, payment system last.

qs.q: What does 'not just a vague promise' imply Priya wants?
opts: A concrete rollback plan for each phase
qs.why: She wants a specific, documented plan, not a general assurance.

script: Let's talk about inflation, because it affects everyone, even if we don't always notice it. Inflation simply means that, over time, prices rise, so the same amount of money buys fewer goods and services. If prices go up by three percent a year, something that costs a hundred dollars today will cost about a hundred and three dollars next year. This is why keeping all your savings in a drawer isn't a good long-term strategy. Your money loses purchasing power, even though the number on the bills stays the same. Many people try to protect their savings by investing, but investing comes with risk, and returns are never guaranteed. A sensible approach is to spread your money across different options and to think carefully about how long you can leave it untouched.

script: Education officials have published new guidelines on the use of artificial intelligence in secondary schools. script: Cybersecurity experts are reminding travellers to be careful when using public Wi-Fi networks in airports, cafés and hotels. These networks are often open, which means other users on the same connection may be able to intercept unprotected data. Experts recommend avoiding online banking or shopping on a public network unless you use a virtual private network, known as a VPN, which encrypts your traffic. They also advise checking the exact name of the network with staff, because criminals sometimes create fake hotspots with similar names. Finally, travellers should keep their phone and laptop software up to date, since updates often fix known security weaknesses. Using your mobile data instead is usually a safer choice for sensitive tasks.

qs.q: Why can public Wi-Fi be risky?
opts: Other users may intercept unprotected data
qs.why: Open networks may let other users intercept unprotected data.

qs.q: Why should travellers check the network name with staff?
opts: To avoid paying for the service
To avoid fake hotspots with similar names
qs.why: Criminals sometimes create fake hotspots with similar names.

qs.q: What does a VPN do, according to the report?
qs.why: The report says a VPN encrypts your traffic.

script: For years, I wore my exhaustion like a badge of honor. I answered emails at midnight, skipped vacations, and believed that being constantly available proved my commitment. Then, one winter, I realized I could no longer concentrate, and small tasks felt overwhelming. It turned out to be burnout, and recovering took months. What surprised me most was how little my absence disrupted the team. The work continued, and my colleagues managed perfectly well. Since returning, I've set firm boundaries: I switch off notifications after six, I take my full vacation, and I say no to projects that I can't realistically finish. Ironically, my performance has improved. I've come to see rest not as a reward for productivity, but as a prerequisite for it.

qs.q: What did the speaker used to believe?
opts: Rest is a waste of time
qs.why: He believed that being constantly available proved his commitment.

qs.q: What surprised the speaker most?
opts: The team managed well without him
qs.why: He was surprised how little his absence disrupted the team.

qs.q: What conclusion does the speaker reach?
opts: Rest is a reward for good results
Rest is a requirement for productivity
qs.why: He sees rest as a prerequisite for productivity, not a reward.

script: Whenever a company announces a data breach, people assume the attackers used some brilliant zero-day exploit.
